title: Finite stages of enumerable sets

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: 25–27 (§§4.1–4.2, finite approximations, increasing enumerations and settling bounds); version 2024-02-25

summary: Approximate enumerable sets by finite computable stages, extract an infinite decidable subset, and characterize decision procedures by increasing enumerations and settling bounds.
abstract: A search can keep reporting new members of a set without ever announcing that its list is complete. Looking at finitely many computations at a time makes these discoveries into finite snapshots, but a quiet snapshot cannot certify permanent absence. Ordering the output changes what can be learned: an infinite set has a decision procedure exactly when a terminating program can list all its members in strictly increasing order. Even when the whole enumerable set is undecidable, selecting successive record highs yields an infinite subset that is decidable. For any fixed computable sequence of growing finite snapshots, deciding the whole set is equivalent to computing a stage by which all discoveries below a given input bound have occurred.
